lesson.title: The Line Must Be Earned
lesson.hook: The open line tempts you from a low ball you're late for, and leaves your whole court open.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time the line opens, check contact height and your time before taking it.

pro.label: Federer v Nadal, Australian Open 2017 final
pro.moment: Second set, 30/40: Nadal went all-out on a forehand down the line, and Federer flicked a forehand back into the open court to break.
pro.read: The line can open the reply behind you.

drill.name: Crosscourt until earned
drill.how: Rally crosscourt. You may change to the line only off a waist-high ball you're set for. A line attempt from a low ball, or one you're late for, loses the point, in or out.

lesson.cue: Heavy crosscourt until I earn the line.

steps.name: Low and late
steps.sit: The line is open, but their low crosscourt pulls you wide, and you're late.
steps.q: Is this the ball to go down the line?
opts: Yes: drive it deep down the line
steps.payoff: The court was open. Your contact wasn't.
steps.principle: Low and late hasn't earned the line.
steps.why: Crosscourt gives you more court, a lower net and time to recover. The line asks a difficult ball to do even more.
steps.take: Low and late? Crosscourt first — the line can wait.

lines.A: Low, late and at the line — only 5 in 10 land. Too much risk for what it wins.
lines.B: Short through the middle — they step in and hit where you're not.
lines.C: Crosscourt gives you net, court and time — you're back in the rally.
lines.D: Short and soft — it sits up, and they step in and punish it.

steps.name: Waist-high and balanced
steps.sit: The next crosscourt lands shorter. You meet it waist-high and balanced.
opts: Down the line, well inside it
steps.payoff: Now the line is on — not compulsory.
steps.principle: Height and balance earn the line. Judgement still picks the target.
steps.why: The shorter ball lets you set up and meet it waist-high. Now the line stretches them. Keep a margin: down the line gives you less court.
steps.take: Waist-high and balanced: the line is on — take it with margin.

lines.A: Safe, but the line was on — the rally just goes on.
lines.B: Down the line, well inside it — they scramble, and the reply is yours.
lines.C: Flat and hard — 3 in 10 miss, and the ones that land come back.
lines.D: High through the middle gives them back their time.

steps.name: Late on the forehand
steps.sit: Their crosscourt pulls you wide on your forehand, and you're late again.
steps.payoff: Different wing, same problem: late and wide hasn't earned the line.
steps.principle: Whether the line is on depends on the ball, not the wing.
steps.why: The forehand may feel stronger, but a ball you're late for still costs control. Crosscourt gives you net, court and time.
steps.take: Late and wide? Either wing — crosscourt, then recover.

lines.A: Late, at the line — only 6 in 10 land, and the ones that do don't hurt them.
lines.B: Short crosscourt sits up — they step in and punish it.
lines.C: Short through the middle — they step in and hit where you're not.
lines.D: Crosscourt buys the time to get back — you're back in the rally.
